title: AP Computer Science Principles
description: Free AP Computer Science Principles study guide: 8 units, 155 practice questions, 80 flashcards, quick reference, memory tricks, and a full practice exam. Completely free.

units.name: Creative Development

concepts.intro: Programs are built by people working together through planning, testing and revision.
b: Collaboration brings diverse perspectives, skills and feedback, which improves the quality of a program.
Development processes are often iterative: design, prototype, test, get feedback and revise, repeating the cycle.
Incremental development builds and tests small pieces one at a time; pair programming has two people share one computer.
Documenting and commenting code helps others and your future self understand what the program does.

concepts.intro: Good programs begin with a clear purpose and are tested with real users.
b: A program's purpose is the problem it solves or the interest it satisfies; requirements describe what it must do.
Input comes from users or other programs; output is what the program produces; user interface design shapes how people interact.
Testing with varied users and inputs finds problems; user feedback guides improvements.
A computing innovation can have intended and unintended effects, both beneficial and harmful.

concepts.intro: Programmers expect errors and use strategies to find and fix them.
b: Syntax errors break the rules of the language; logic errors make the program run but give wrong results; runtime errors occur while running.
Overflow errors occur when a value is larger than the computer can store; round-off errors come from limited precision for real numbers.
Debugging strategies: test with different inputs, hand-trace the code, add display statements, and test small segments in isolation.

traps: A program that runs without crashing can still contain a logic error; testing must check the output, not just that it ran.
Collaboration does not mean everyone writes every line; roles and communication matter.

units.name: Data Representation

concepts.intro: Computers represent all information using bits, each either 0 or 1.
b: A bit is a single binary digit; a byte is 8 bits. With n bits you can represent 2^n different values (n bits count from 0 up to 2^n - 1).
Binary place values from the right are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128; add the place values that have a 1 to convert to decimal.
Using more bits lets you represent more values or finer detail; the same bits can represent numbers, text, colors or sound depending on the interpretation.
Overflow happens when a number exceeds the largest value the bits can hold.

concepts.intro: All kinds of data are encoded as bits using agreed-upon formats.
b: Text uses character encodings such as ASCII and Unicode; Unicode represents characters from many languages.
Images are grids of pixels; each pixel's color is stored as numbers, commonly red, green and blue values (RGB).
Sound is sampled at regular intervals; a higher sampling rate and more bits per sample give higher quality and larger files.
Analog data is continuous; digitizing samples it, which may lose some detail.

concepts.intro: Compression reduces the number of bits needed to store or send data.
b: Lossless compression allows the original data to be reconstructed exactly (PNG, ZIP, FLAC); lossy compression discards some data for smaller files (JPEG, MP3).
Lossless is needed when exact data matters (text, programs); lossy is acceptable when small losses are not noticeable.
Metadata is data about data, such as the date a photo was taken; it can reveal information you did not intend to share.

traps: The number of values with n bits is 2 to the n, but the largest value is 2^n minus 1 because counting starts at 0.
Lossy compression cannot restore the original data; lossless can.

units.name: Data Analysis and Big Data

concepts.intro: Data can be examined for patterns and used to draw conclusions.
b: Data is raw facts; information is the useful meaning extracted from data; patterns and trends in data support decisions.
Correlation does not imply causation: two variables can move together without one causing the other.
Bias in how data is collected or who is included can lead to misleading conclusions.
Visualizations such as charts and graphs help people see patterns.

concepts.intro: Computers can analyze extremely large collections of data.
b: Big data sets are too large for traditional tools; they are processed using parallel and distributed computing.
Data sets may be incomplete, contain errors or be biased, so data must be cleaned before analysis.
Scalability describes how well a system handles growth in data or users.
Using data to make decisions raises privacy concerns about how data is collected, stored and shared.

concepts.intro: Programs filter, sort and combine data to answer questions.
b: Filtering selects the data that meet a condition; sorting arranges data in order; transforming changes data into another form.
Combining data sets can reveal new information but can also compromise privacy by re-identifying individuals.
Spreadsheets and databases store and process structured data.

traps: A strong correlation is not proof of cause.
Anonymized data can sometimes be re-identified when combined with other data sets.

units.name: Algorithms

concepts.intro: An algorithm is a finite set of instructions that accomplishes a task.
b: Every algorithm can be built from three constructs: sequencing (steps in order), selection (choosing with conditions) and iteration (repeating).
Different algorithms can solve the same problem with different efficiency.
Algorithms are expressed in natural language, flowcharts or pseudocode before being coded.

concepts.intro: Efficiency compares how the resources needed grow with the size of the input.
b: Linear (sequential) search checks each element in turn and works on unsorted data; binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list and is much faster.
Binary search needs the data to be sorted; each step eliminates half of the remaining items.
An algorithm runs in reasonable time if the steps grow as a polynomial (such as n or n squared) of the input size; exponential growth is unreasonable.
Some problems are undecidable: no algorithm can solve them for all inputs (the halting problem).

concepts.intro: When exact solutions are impractical, approximations and models help.
b: A heuristic finds an approximate solution quickly when an exact one would take too long.
Simulations model real-world systems, allowing experiments that are costly or dangerous; they simplify reality and may leave out factors.
Randomness is used in simulations and games; results vary each run.

traps: Binary search only works on sorted data.
A faster-looking algorithm is not always better if the data is small; efficiency matters as input size grows.

units.name: Programming

concepts.intro: Programs store values in variables and combine them with operators.
b: A variable stores a value that can change; assignment in the AP language is written with an arrow, for example x ← 5.
Arithmetic operators are +, -, *, / and MOD (the remainder); MOD is used to test divisibility and to wrap around.
A list is an ordered collection; in the AP language list indexes start at 1; APPEND adds, INSERT puts an item at an index, REMOVE deletes, LENGTH returns the number of items.
Strings are sequences of characters; concatenation joins strings.

concepts.intro: Control structures determine which statements run and how many times.
b: Boolean values are true or false; relational operators (=, ≠, >, <, ≥, ≤) and logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) form conditions.
IF/ELSE selects between paths; nested conditionals test further conditions.
REPEAT n TIMES runs a block a set number of times; REPEAT UNTIL runs until a condition becomes true; FOR EACH item IN list visits each element.
Careful tracing of loops tracks the value of each variable after every iteration.

concepts.intro: Procedures organize code into reusable named blocks.
b: A procedure (function) has a name, optional parameters and may return a value; calling it runs the code with given arguments.
Procedural abstraction hides details so you can use a procedure without knowing how it works, which makes programs easier to write and maintain.
Libraries and APIs provide existing code; using them speeds development; RANDOM(a, b) returns a random integer from a to b inclusive.
Parameters make a procedure general; global and local variables differ in where they can be used.

traps: In the AP pseudocode, list indexes start at 1, not 0.
MOD gives the remainder, not the quotient; 17 MOD 5 is 2.

units.name: Computer Systems and the Internet

concepts.l: The Internet and how data travels
concepts.intro: The Internet is a network of networks using shared protocols.
b: A computing device sends data in packets, small chunks that are routed independently and reassembled at the destination.
Protocols such as IP (addressing and routing), TCP (reliable delivery) and HTTP (web pages) are open standards that let different systems communicate.
The Domain Name System (DNS) translates domain names into IP addresses.
Bandwidth is the maximum amount of data per second; latency is the delay; a download time is the file size divided by the bandwidth.

concepts.intro: The Internet is designed to keep working when parts fail.
b: Routing is dynamic: routers choose paths, and redundant paths mean data can be rerouted around failures (fault tolerance).
Redundancy improves reliability but costs more resources.
The Internet is scalable because the protocols let new devices and networks join without central control.

concepts.intro: Splitting work across processors can speed up computation.
b: Sequential computing runs one step at a time; parallel computing runs parts simultaneously on multiple processors; distributed computing uses multiple devices.
Speedup is the time of sequential execution divided by the time of parallel execution.
Not all tasks can be parallelized; steps that depend on earlier results must wait.
Parallel solutions can solve problems that would be too large for a single computer.

traps: The Internet and the World Wide Web are not the same: the web is a service that runs on the Internet.
Bandwidth is a maximum rate, while latency is delay.

units.name: Cybersecurity and Privacy

concepts.intro: Cybersecurity protects data and systems from unauthorized access.
b: Phishing tricks people into revealing information; keylogging records keystrokes; malware is malicious software; rogue access points imitate trusted networks.
A distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack overwhelms a service with traffic from many devices.
Strong, unique passwords and multifactor authentication reduce the risk of account takeover.

concepts.intro: Encryption protects information by making it unreadable without a key.
b: Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt; public-key (asymmetric) encryption uses a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt.
Public-key encryption lets people who have never met exchange secure messages; it underlies HTTPS.
Certificate authorities help verify that a website's public key belongs to the claimed owner.

concepts.intro: Collecting and sharing data creates privacy risks.
b: Personally identifiable information (PII) is data that can identify a person, such as a name or address.
Websites and apps collect data through cookies, location services and user accounts; users can review privacy settings.
Combining multiple data sets can reveal identities even when each alone seems harmless.

traps: Encryption does not hide that a message exists; it protects the contents.
In public-key encryption the public key can be shared widely, but the private key must stay secret.

units.name: Impact of Computing

concepts.intro: Computing innovations affect society in many ways, some unintended.
b: Innovations can transform health care, education and communication but may also cause harm, such as job displacement or privacy loss.
The digital divide is the gap between people with and without access to computers and the Internet; it can widen inequality.
Computing bias arises when data or design reflects human prejudice, for example in facial recognition or hiring algorithms.

concepts.intro: Large groups of people can contribute data and solve problems.
b: Crowdsourcing gathers contributions from many people online; citizen science lets volunteers help with research.
Open data sets and open-source software share work widely; contributors benefit from many perspectives.

concepts.intro: Intellectual property and licensing govern how work can be used.
b: Copyright protects creators; Creative Commons licenses let creators allow certain uses of their work.
Open-source software lets anyone view and modify the code; licenses specify the conditions.
Citing sources and obtaining permission respects the rights of creators; plagiarism is presenting others' work as your own.
Computing has an energy footprint; data centers consume large amounts of electricity.

traps: Using data or an algorithm does not make a decision objective; bias in the data can be reproduced by the program.
Free to view does not mean free to reuse; check the license.

quiz.q: A team builds a program by designing a prototype, testing it with users, and then revising it repeatedly. This is an example of:
o: A waterfall process
Random testing
An iterative development process
Sequential execution
quiz.e: Iterative development repeats the cycle of design, test, feedback and revision.

quiz.q: Which is the main benefit of collaboration when developing a program?
o: It guarantees that the finished program will contain no bugs at all
Different perspectives and skills improve the quality of the solution
It removes the need for testing because teammates check every line
It makes the finished program shorter and faster for every user
quiz.e: Diverse viewpoints help catch problems and generate better ideas.

quiz.q: In pair programming, two programmers:
o: Write the same program separately and then compare the two versions
Work together at one computer, one writing code and the other reviewing
Divide the program so that each programmer writes exactly half of it
Test each other's computers to find hardware problems before coding
quiz.e: The reviewer catches mistakes as the other types.

quiz.q: Which statement best describes the purpose of a program?
o: The programming language and tools used to write the code
The total number of lines of code in the finished program
The processing speed of the computer that runs the program
The problem it solves or the interest it satisfies for its users
quiz.e: Purpose guides the requirements and design.

quiz.q: A program is incorrect because it adds numbers instead of multiplying them, but it runs without any error message. This is a:
o: Syntax error
Runtime error
Logic error
Overflow error
quiz.e: The code follows the rules of the language but does not do what was intended.

quiz.q: A program fails to run because a line is missing a closing parenthesis. This is a:
o: Logic error
Syntax error
Round-off error
Overflow error
quiz.e: Syntax errors violate the rules of the language.

quiz.q: A program crashes when it tries to divide by zero while running. This is a:
o: Runtime error
Syntax error
Logic error
Compile-time error
quiz.e: The error occurs while the program is executing.

quiz.q: Which strategy would help a programmer find a logic error?
o: Deleting the program and rewriting it from scratch without any testing
Running the program one time and assuming it works for all input
Changing the font and colors of the editor to spot mistakes
Hand-tracing the code with sample input and checking each step
quiz.e: Tracing shows where actual behavior differs from the intended behavior.

quiz.q: Adding DISPLAY statements to show the value of variables during execution is a technique used for:
o: Compressing
Encrypting
Debugging
Sorting
quiz.e: Seeing values helps locate where a program goes wrong.

quiz.q: Which is the best reason to test a program with a variety of inputs?
o: To make the program run faster for every possible kind of input
To find errors that appear only for certain values
To reduce the number of variables the program needs to store
To avoid having to write comments explaining each procedure
quiz.e: Edge cases and unusual inputs reveal bugs.

quiz.q: Comments in code are useful because they:
o: Make the program run faster because the computer reads them first
Are required by the computer in order for the code to execute
Explain the code's purpose to other programmers and to your future self
Replace the need for testing by proving the code is correct
quiz.e: Comments are ignored by the computer but help people understand.

quiz.q: A program is considered to have an unintended effect when it:
o: Runs exactly as designed and produces only the planned results
Produces a result the creators did not plan, which may be harmful
Is fully documented so that every behavior has been described
Has been tested thoroughly and passes every planned test case
quiz.e: Innovations can have beneficial and harmful unintended consequences.

quiz.q: In developing a program, user feedback is most useful for:
o: Making the program longer by adding as many features as possible
Choosing which programming language the program should use
Identifying problems and improving the design
Compressing the program's data so that it takes less storage
quiz.e: Real users reveal usability problems designers may not anticipate.

quiz.q: An overflow error occurs when:
o: A calculated value is too large to be stored with the available bits
A program has too few comments to describe all of its procedures
The user enters text where the program expected a number
A loop never begins because its condition is false at the start
quiz.e: Computers store numbers using a fixed number of bits.

quiz.q: Incremental development means:
o: Building and testing a program in small pieces
Writing all of the code first and then testing it only once
Testing only at the very end after the program is finished
Using only one large function for the entire program
quiz.e: Small steps make it easier to find and fix problems.

quiz.q: The input to a program is:
o: The result displayed
The code itself
The compiler
Data provided to the program
quiz.e: Input can come from users, files or other programs.

quiz.q: How many different values can be represented using 5 bits?
quiz.e: With n bits there are 2^n values: 2^5 = 32.

quiz.q: What is the largest decimal value that can be stored using 8 bits?
quiz.e: The values run from 0 to 2^8 - 1 = 255.

quiz.q: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1011?
What is the binary representation of the decimal number 10?
quiz.e: 10 = 8 + 2, so the bits for 8 and 2 are 1.

quiz.q: What is the minimum number of bits needed to represent 20 different values?
quiz.e: Four bits give 16 values, not enough; five bits give 32.

quiz.q: A byte is made up of how many bits?
quiz.e: A byte is 8 bits.

quiz.q: An overflow error in a computer that stores integers with a fixed number of bits occurs when:
o: A number being stored is negative instead of positive
A bit in the stored value happens to be 0 instead of 1
A result is larger than the maximum value the bits can store
A number being stored happens to be even rather than odd
quiz.e: The result cannot be represented with the available bits.

quiz.q: Which of the following best explains why a computer can use bits to represent text, images and sound?
o: Bits automatically know which kind of data they represent without any rules
Different kinds of data are encoded using agreed-upon rules for interpreting bits
Each type of data is stored using a different kind of hardware
Only numbers can be stored in bits, so text is converted to math
quiz.e: The meaning of a bit sequence depends on the encoding used.

quiz.q: Unicode is an improvement over ASCII because it:
o: Uses fewer bits for every character so files are smaller
Can represent characters from many more languages
Runs faster because computers process it more quickly than ASCII
Stores images and sounds in addition to text characters
quiz.e: ASCII has only 128 characters.

quiz.q: An image is stored as a grid of colored dots called:
o: Bytes
Samples
Pixels
Packets
quiz.e: Each pixel's color is stored as numbers.

quiz.q: In the RGB color model, what color does (255, 0, 0) represent?
o: Green
Red
Blue
White
quiz.e: The first value is the amount of red.

quiz.q: Increasing the sampling rate when digitizing sound will generally:
o: Decrease the quality while the file size stays the same
Decrease the file size only, with no change in sound quality
Have no effect on either the quality or the file size
Increase the quality and the file size
quiz.e: More samples per second capture the sound wave more accurately.

quiz.q: Lossless compression:
o: Allows the original data to be perfectly reconstructed
Permanently removes some data so that files become much smaller
Always creates smaller files than lossy compression does
Works only for images and cannot be used on text or sound
quiz.e: No information is lost.

quiz.q: Which type of file is most likely to use lossy compression?
o: A ZIP archive of text
A program file
A JPEG photograph
A spreadsheet of numbers
quiz.e: Small image detail losses are often not noticeable.

quiz.q: A programmer needs to compress a text document so that the original text can be recovered exactly. Which should be used?
o: Lossy compression
Lossless compression
No compression is possible
Analog conversion
quiz.e: Text must be restored exactly.

quiz.q: Metadata is:
o: Data that describes other data
The main content of a file
A type of virus
A compression algorithm
quiz.e: An example is the date and location stored with a photo.

quiz.q: Digitizing an analog signal by sampling may:
o: Create a perfect copy
Increase file size to infinity
Remove all noise
Lose some detail between samples
quiz.e: Samples approximate a continuous signal.

quiz.q: Which of the following sets of values requires the fewest bits to represent?
o: The months of the year
The letters of the alphabet
The days of the week
The numbers from 1 to 100
quiz.e: Seven values need 3 bits; the others need more.

quiz.q: A computer represents the decimal number 7 in binary as:
A study finds that cities with more ice cream shops also have more sunburn cases. Which conclusion is best supported?
o: The two variables are correlated, but this alone does not show one causes the other
Ice cream consumption directly causes people to get sunburned
Sunburn cases cause people to buy more ice cream in those cities
The data must be wrong because the two variables are unrelated
quiz.e: A third factor, such as sunny weather, can influence both.

quiz.q: Which of the following describes big data?
o: Data sets stored in a very large spreadsheet that opens slowly
Data collected only by computers that have very large screens
Data sets so large that they require special tools such as parallel processing
Any data stored in a single file on one computer's hard drive
quiz.e: Big data is too large or complex for traditional tools.

quiz.q: A researcher collects data only from people who have a smartphone. The most likely problem is:
o: Overflow, because the number of responses is too large to store
Lossy compression, because some details of the data were removed
Sampling bias, because the data may not represent everyone
Too few bits, because the data cannot be stored accurately
quiz.e: People without smartphones are left out.

quiz.q: Cleaning a data set means:
o: Compressing the data so that it takes up less storage space
Encrypting the data so that unauthorized people cannot read it
Fixing or removing errors, duplicates and inconsistent values
Making the data private by removing names and personal details
quiz.e: Data quality affects the reliability of analysis.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of filtering data?
o: Sorting the names in the data set into alphabetical order
Selecting only the rows where the age is over 18
Adding a new column that is calculated from existing columns
Encrypting the file so that only authorized users can open it
quiz.e: Filtering keeps the data that meet a condition.

quiz.q: A company combines two anonymous data sets and is able to identify individual people. This illustrates:
o: A privacy risk of combining data sets
Lossless compression
Benefits of encryption
Overflow
quiz.e: Combining sources can re-identify individuals.

quiz.q: A scatterplot of two variables shows that as one increases, the other tends to increase. This is a:
o: Negative correlation
No correlation
Causation
Positive correlation
quiz.e: The variables move in the same direction.

quiz.q: Scalability of a system refers to its ability to:
o: Run on any computer
Compress files
Handle growth in data or users
Encrypt messages
quiz.e: A scalable system continues to work well as demand increases.

quiz.q: Why are visualizations such as charts useful in analyzing data?
o: They remove the need to collect any data in the first place
They compress the data so that it takes less storage space
They make patterns and trends easier to see
They encrypt the data so that it cannot be read by others
quiz.e: Humans recognize patterns visually.

quiz.q: A program sorts a list of 1,000,000 records. Which statement is true?
o: The program can process the records much faster than a person can
The program must be run by hand because computers cannot sort that many
The records cannot be sorted because the list is far too long
Sorting always takes exactly 1,000,000 steps no matter the method
quiz.e: Computers process large data sets quickly.

quiz.q: Which is a potential issue when using data to make decisions?
o: Data is always accurate
Data cannot be analyzed
Data is never useful
The data may be biased or incomplete
quiz.e: Decisions are only as good as the data.

quiz.q: A spreadsheet has a column of dates and a column of sales. Which analysis would show how sales change over time?
o: A list of dates alone
Sorting by the sales column only
A line graph of sales by date
Deleting the dates
quiz.e: A time series shows trends.

quiz.q: Transforming data means:
o: Deleting the data once it has been analyzed and is not needed
Encrypting the data so that it can be sent over a network
Changing it into another form, such as converting units
Copying the data to a second location as a backup
quiz.e: For example, converting Celsius to Fahrenheit.

quiz.q: Why can a large data set still lead to a wrong conclusion?
o: It may be biased or may not represent the question being asked
Large data sets are always correct because of the amount of data
Computers cannot process data sets that contain so many records
Large data sets never contain any patterns that can be found
quiz.e: Size does not guarantee quality.

quiz.q: A health app collects location data. Which is the biggest privacy concern?
o: The app uses bright colors that may distract its users
The app is free, so it must earn money in other ways
The data could reveal where a person lives and goes
The app has many users, which slows down its servers
quiz.e: Location patterns are highly personal.

quiz.q: Which of the following are the three basic building blocks of every algorithm?
o: Input, output and storage
Variables, lists and strings
Compile, run and debug
Sequencing, selection and iteration
quiz.e: All algorithms can be built from these constructs.

quiz.q: Which search algorithm requires the data to be sorted?
o: Linear search
Both
Binary search
Neither
quiz.e: Binary search relies on order to eliminate half the items each step.

quiz.q: A sorted list contains 1,000 items. About how many comparisons does binary search need in the worst case?
o: About 1000
About 10
About 500
About 100
quiz.e: 2^10 is 1024, so about 10 halvings.

quiz.q: A linear search of an unsorted list of 500 items checks, in the worst case:
o: 500 items
10 items
250 items
1 item
quiz.e: The target may be last or absent.

quiz.q: Which of the following algorithms runs in a reasonable time?
o: One whose steps grow as 2 to the n
One that tries every possible arrangement of a large input
One that never ends
One whose steps grow as n squared
quiz.e: Polynomial growth is considered reasonable; exponential growth is not.

quiz.q: A heuristic is used when:
o: An exact answer is easy to compute, so approximation is unnecessary
An exact solution would take too long, so an approximate solution is acceptable
The data has already been sorted, so searching is quick
No computer is available, so the problem must be solved by hand
quiz.e: Heuristics trade accuracy for speed.

quiz.q: Which of the following is true of a simulation?
o: It is always exactly like reality and includes every detail
It models a real system and can leave out details
It cannot include any randomness or unpredictable events
It requires no data because the results are made up
quiz.e: Simplifications help explore scenarios safely and cheaply.

quiz.q: An algorithm that works for all inputs is said to be:
o: Correct
Heuristic
Lossy
Sequential
quiz.e: Correctness means it produces the right result for every valid input.

quiz.q: A problem for which no algorithm can produce a correct answer for all inputs is called:
o: Unreasonable
Sorted
Heuristic
Undecidable
quiz.e: The halting problem is a famous example.

quiz.q: Two algorithms solve the same problem. Algorithm A takes 10n steps and Algorithm B takes n squared steps. For large n, which is more efficient?
o: Algorithm B
They are equal
Algorithm A
It depends on the computer
quiz.e: Linear growth is slower than quadratic growth.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a benefit of using pseudocode before writing a program?
o: It helps plan the logic independent of a programming language
It makes the finished program run faster on any computer
It compresses the code so that the program uses less memory
It encrypts the program's data so that it stays secure
quiz.e: Pseudocode lets you focus on the algorithm.

quiz.q: A flowchart is used to:
o: Compress files so that they take up less storage space
Show the steps and decisions in an algorithm visually
Encrypt data so that others cannot read it while it travels
Store data in rows and columns so it can be searched later
quiz.e: Shapes represent actions and decisions.

quiz.q: Which situation is best modeled with a simulation?
o: Testing how a disease might spread through a population
Adding two numbers that the user has typed into a form
Sorting a long list of names into alphabetical order
Checking the spelling of words in a typed document
quiz.e: Simulations let people explore outcomes without real-world risk.

quiz.q: Using random numbers in a simulation means that:
o: Results are always identical every time it runs
The program cannot run because computers cannot be random
The simulation is wrong and its results should be ignored
Results may differ each time it runs
quiz.e: Randomness introduces variation.

quiz.q: Selection in an algorithm means:
o: Repeating a group of steps until a condition is met
Running the steps one after another in the order written
Ending the algorithm once all of the data is processed
Choosing between paths based on a condition
quiz.e: IF statements implement selection.

quiz.q:
What is displayed?

x ← 4
y ← x * 2 + 1
DISPLAY(y)

quiz.q: Which expression is true when the whole number n is even?
o: n MOD 2 = 1
n MOD 10 = 2
n MOD 2 = 0

quiz.q: In the AP pseudocode, the first element of a list named myList is accessed with:
o: myList[0]

myList[1]
myList(0)

What is the value of LENGTH(aList) after these statements?

INSERT(aList, 2, 9)

}

}

quiz.e: n takes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; the loop stops when n is 32.

sum ← 0
FOR EACH item IN [2, 4, 6]
{
 sum ← sum + item
}
DISPLAY(sum)

o: A
B
AB
Nothing
quiz.e: The condition 7 > 5 is true.

quiz.q: The expression (a > 3) AND (b < 5) is true when:
o: Either condition is true
Neither condition is true
a is less than b
Both conditions are true
quiz.e: AND requires both operands to be true.

quiz.q: The expression NOT (x = 4) is true when:
o: x equals 4
x is greater than 4
x is any value other than 4
x is positive
quiz.e: NOT reverses the Boolean value.

quiz.q: If a = true and b = false, what is the value of (a OR b) AND (NOT b)?
o: false
true
undefined
b
quiz.e: (true OR false) is true and NOT false is true, so true AND true is true.
The procedure returns twice its parameter.

quiz.q: Which is the main advantage of procedural abstraction?
o: It makes every program run faster by shortening the code
It removes the need for variables in a program
It reduces the number of bits needed to store data
A procedure can be used without knowing the details of how it works
quiz.e: Abstraction manages complexity.

quiz.q: Which statement about parameters is true?
o: A procedure may have only one parameter, which must be a number
Parameters are the values that a procedure sends back when it ends
Parameters must always be numbers and cannot be strings or lists
Parameters let a procedure work with different input values each time it is called
quiz.e: Parameters make procedures reusable.

quiz.q: A programmer uses a library of existing procedures. This most directly:
o: Slows the program down because the library code is not efficient
Removes the need to test the program since the library works
Saves development time by reusing tested code
Encrypts the code so that other people cannot copy it
quiz.e: Libraries and APIs provide ready-made functionality.

quiz.q: What are the possible values of RANDOM(1, 6)?
o: Integers from 1 to 6, inclusive
Integers from 1 to 5
Decimals between 1 and 6
Only 1 and 6
quiz.e: The AP RANDOM procedure includes both endpoints.

quiz.q: Concatenating the strings "net" and "work" gives:
o: "net work"
"netwo"
"work net"
"network"
quiz.e: Concatenation joins the strings end to end.

quiz.q: A loop that never ends is called:
o: A nested loop
A recursive loop
An infinite loop
A conditional
quiz.e: The condition never becomes true (or false) to stop it.

quiz.q: On the Internet, a message is typically divided into:
o: One continuous stream that travels along a single path
Pixels that are sent separately and combined on screen
Bits that must travel together along the same route
Packets that may take different routes
quiz.e: Packets are reassembled at the destination.

quiz.q: The role of the Domain Name System (DNS) is to:
o: Encrypt messages so that only the receiver can read them
Compress files so that they travel faster across the network
Translate domain names into IP addresses
Store web pages so that they load more quickly later
quiz.e: Computers route using IP addresses, not names.

quiz.q: Which protocol is responsible for addressing and routing packets across the Internet?
o: IP
HTTP
HTML
FTP
quiz.e: IP gives each device an address.

quiz.q: Open protocols are important to the Internet because they:
o: Allow different devices and systems to communicate
Keep the Internet private so only approved users connect
Reduce the number of users who can join the network
Compress data so that it travels faster between devices
quiz.e: Anyone can build a system that follows them.

quiz.q: Bandwidth is the:
o: Delay before the first data begins arriving at the receiver
Maximum amount of data that can be sent in a given time
Number of devices that are connected to a network at once
Size of a file measured in bytes after it is compressed
quiz.e: Latency is the delay.

quiz.q: A 12 megabyte file is downloaded over a connection with a bandwidth of 3 megabytes per second. About how long will it take?
o: 36 seconds
4 seconds
15 seconds
0.25 seconds
quiz.e: 12 divided by 3 is 4 seconds.

quiz.q: A network has multiple paths between devices. If one path fails, data can use another. This property is called:
o: Fault tolerance
Compression
Encryption
Parallelism
quiz.e: Redundancy lets the network keep working.

quiz.q: Which statement about the Internet and the World Wide Web is correct?
o: They are exactly the same thing and the terms can be swapped
The Internet is a service that runs on top of the web
The web is a service that runs on the Internet
The web is a type of protocol only and not a service
quiz.e: The Internet is the network; the web is one use of it.

quiz.q: A task takes 60 seconds on one processor and 20 seconds when split across several processors. The speedup is:
quiz.e: Speedup = sequential time divided by parallel time.

quiz.q: Which task is least suited to parallel computing?
o: One that processes millions of independent records separately
One in which each step depends on the result of the previous step
One that renders separate frames of a video at the same time
One that searches separate sections of a data set at once
quiz.e: Dependent steps must run in order.

quiz.q: Distributed computing is the use of:
o: Multiple devices working together to solve a problem
One very fast computer solving the problem all by itself
Only parallel processors that are located inside one chip
A single network cable carrying data between two computers
quiz.e: Distributed systems share work across machines.

quiz.q: The Internet's design makes it scalable because:
o: Only a small, fixed number of devices are allowed to connect
A central computer controls and approves all of the traffic
New devices and networks can join without a central authority
Each device is limited to a single connection at one time
quiz.e: Shared protocols allow growth.

quiz.q: Packets are numbered so that they can:
o: Be reassembled in the correct order at the destination
Be encrypted so that no one can read them in transit
Be compressed so that they take less time to send
Avoid every possible error while they travel to the destination
quiz.e: Packets may arrive out of order.

quiz.q: A computer sends a request to a web server and waits several seconds before a page begins to load. This delay is mostly:
o: Bandwidth
Latency
Compression
Encryption
quiz.e: Latency is the time delay.

quiz.q: Which best describes a router?
o: A device that forwards packets toward their destination
A device that stores web pages and sends them to browsers
A device that compresses files so they are smaller to send
A program that edits images before they are posted online
quiz.e: Routers decide the next hop for each packet.

quiz.q: Using redundant routing on the Internet generally:
o: Decreases reliability because data is split over many paths
Makes the Internet slower for everyone who uses it
Increases reliability but uses more resources
Eliminates the need for protocols because paths are guaranteed
quiz.e: Extra paths provide backups.

quiz.q: An email appears to be from a bank and asks you to click a link and enter your password. This is an example of:
o: Compression
Parallel computing
Debugging
Phishing
quiz.e: Phishing tricks people into revealing sensitive information.

quiz.q: A DDoS attack is intended to:
o: Steal passwords by tricking users into typing them on a fake site
Encrypt data on a server until the owner pays a ransom
Fix bugs in a service by sending it many test requests
Overwhelm a service with traffic so legitimate users cannot access it
quiz.e: Many devices send traffic at once.

quiz.q: Which practice most improves the security of an online account?
o: Using the same easy-to-remember password for every account
Sharing the password only with close friends and family
Using a unique, strong password with multifactor authentication
Using a short password that is simple to type quickly
quiz.e: Layered protection reduces risk.

quiz.q: Malware is:
o: A type of compression that makes large files smaller to send
Software intended to damage or gain unauthorized access to a system
A programming language used for writing web pages
A kind of network that connects computers in one building
quiz.e: Viruses and ransomware are examples.

quiz.q: In symmetric encryption:
o: The same key is used to encrypt and decrypt
Two different keys are used, one public and one private
No key is used because the message is only scrambled
The key is made public so anyone can decrypt the message
quiz.e: Both parties must share the secret key.

quiz.q: In public-key encryption, a message encrypted with a person's public key can be decrypted:
o: With the public key
By anyone
Only with that person's private key
With no key
quiz.e: The private key must be kept secret.

quiz.q: A major advantage of public-key encryption is that it:
o: Is much faster than symmetric encryption for large amounts of data
Removes the need for passwords on accounts and devices
Allows secure communication between people who have never shared a secret key
Compresses data so that it travels more quickly across a network
quiz.e: Public keys can be shared openly.

quiz.q: Which protocol uses encryption to secure web traffic?
o: HTTPS
HTTP
FTP
DNS
quiz.e: HTTPS adds encryption to HTTP.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of personally identifiable information (PII)?
o: The color of a website
A public holiday
The weather
A person's home address
quiz.e: PII can be used to identify a person.

quiz.q: A user notices an app is requesting access to location, contacts and microphone even though it needs none to function. The best response is to:
o: Allow all permissions
Share the password
Deny unneeded permissions
Uninstall the operating system
quiz.e: Limit data access to what is needed.

quiz.q: Keylogging software is dangerous because it:
o: Deletes files from the computer so that data is lost
Slows down the computer by using up its processing power
Records what a user types, including passwords
Compresses data so that the user loses some of it
quiz.e: It can capture sensitive information.

quiz.q: A rogue access point is:
o: A type of router that is used to extend a home network
A secure network that encrypts all of the data sent on it
A backup connection that is used when the main one fails
A fake wireless network that imitates a trusted one to capture data
quiz.e: Users may connect without realizing.

quiz.q: Multifactor authentication requires a user to provide:
o: Only a password, but one that is long and hard to guess
Two or more kinds of evidence, such as a password and a code
A longer password with numbers and special characters added
A fingerprint scan only, with no other evidence needed
quiz.e: Multiple factors make theft harder.

quiz.q: Why is it risky to use public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions without protection?
o: Public Wi-Fi is always slow, so transactions often time out
Others on the network might intercept unencrypted data
It uses too much power and drains the battery of the device
It blocks most websites that handle financial information
quiz.e: Encryption such as HTTPS or a VPN reduces the risk.

quiz.q: A cookie on a website is:
o: A virus that spreads from one website to another
A small file that stores information about your visit
A type of compression used to shrink web pages
A password that the website saves for your next visit
quiz.e: Cookies can track preferences and activity.

quiz.q: Combining information from several sources about a person can threaten privacy because:
o: It always deletes the original data once it is combined
It encrypts the data so that no one can read it
It can reveal details no single source would show
It reduces the number of sources that hold information
quiz.e: Aggregation can re-identify individuals.

quiz.q: The digital divide refers to the:
o: Gap between people who have access to computers and the Internet and those who do not
Difference between binary numbers and the decimal numbers people use
Separation of data into packets that travel across a network
Difference in file sizes between images, audio and video
quiz.e: It can increase inequality in education and opportunity.

quiz.q: A facial recognition system works well for some groups but poorly for others. This is most likely due to:
o: A hardware failure
Too much bandwidth
Lossless compression
Bias in the data used to train it
quiz.e: Training data that lacks diversity leads to biased results.

quiz.q: Crowdsourcing is:
o: Encrypting a message so that only a large group can read it
Compressing a file by removing details most people will not notice
Gathering ideas, data or work from a large group of people, often online
Sorting a long list of items by asking a crowd to compare them
quiz.e: Examples include online map editing and review sites.

quiz.q: Citizen science projects use volunteers to:
o: Write operating systems for computers that scientists use
Collect or analyze data for scientific research
Encrypt messages that are sent between research laboratories
Replace scientists so that research can be done without them
quiz.e: Many people can contribute observations.

quiz.q: A Creative Commons license allows a creator to:
o: Remove all copyright so anyone may use the work freely
Specify how others may use and share their work
Force other people to pay a fee whenever they use the work
Hide the work so that only approved users can view it
quiz.e: Different licenses allow different uses.

quiz.q: Open-source software is software that:
o: Is always free of bugs because many people review it
Cannot be used commercially by any company or person
Is stored in the cloud instead of on a local computer
Makes its source code available for others to view and modify
quiz.e: Contributors can improve and share it.

quiz.q: A student copies a paragraph from a website into a report without credit. This is:
o: Crowdsourcing
Open-source collaboration
Plagiarism
Lossy compression
quiz.e: Presenting others' work as your own is plagiarism.

quiz.q: Which is an example of a harmful, unintended effect of a computing innovation?
o: Faster communication
Automated systems displacing workers
Lower costs of storing photos
Online learning access
quiz.e: Innovations can cause problems their creators did not intend.

quiz.q: Why does computing have an environmental impact?
o: Computers make no heat, so they use almost no energy
Data centers and devices consume large amounts of energy
Programs use no electricity once they have been installed
Bits are heavy, so storing more of them requires more material
quiz.e: Energy use contributes to emissions.

quiz.q: A company's hiring algorithm is trained on past hiring decisions that favored one group. The algorithm will most likely:
o: Remove all bias
Hire randomly
Stop working
Reproduce the existing bias
quiz.e: Algorithms can learn the patterns, including prejudiced ones, in their data.

quiz.q: Which is a benefit of open data sets?
o: They are always accurate because so many people use them
They need no cleaning because they are checked before release
Many people can analyze them and find new insights
They eliminate privacy concerns because the data is public
quiz.e: Openness invites more perspectives.

quiz.q: Which action best respects the rights of creators of an image found online?
o: Use it freely without asking because it is posted online
Remove the creator's name so that the image looks cleaner
Check the license and give credit as required
Claim it as your own after making small changes to it
quiz.e: Free to view does not mean free to reuse.

quiz.q: Telemedicine, which allows patients to meet with doctors online, is an example of:
o: A harmful technology only, because it replaces in-person care
A programming language used to build medical software
A compression method used to send medical images quickly
A computing innovation with benefits and potential drawbacks
quiz.e: It increases access but depends on connectivity.

quiz.q: Which of the following best describes how social media algorithms can affect users?
o: They always show random posts that have no link to past behavior
They never use any data about what a user has viewed
They show all posts to every user in exactly the same way
They may show content that reinforces existing views
quiz.e: Recommendations are based on past behavior.

quiz.q: A person with limited Internet access is least likely to be able to:
o: Complete online coursework or apply for jobs online
Read a printed book that was borrowed from a library
Walk to school along a path in the neighborhood
Use a calculator to complete homework problems
quiz.e: Access affects opportunities.

quiz.q: Which is an example of an input to a program?
o: The color of the screen as it is displayed to the user
The name that the programmer gave to the program
A user typing a number into a text box
The speed of the processor that runs the program
quiz.e: Input is data the program receives.

quiz.q: A program displays a message after the user clicks a button. The click is an example of:
o: A bug
An event
A comment
A variable
quiz.e: Events trigger parts of a program.

quiz.q: Rounding errors occur when:
o: A real number cannot be stored exactly with the limited bits available
A number is negative and must be stored with a sign bit
A program has no input from the user to process
A loop is nested inside of another loop in the program
quiz.e: Limited precision causes small differences.

quiz.q: Which best describes a prototype?
o: The final version of a program that is released to users
A comment that explains what a section of code does
A compression format used to store the program's files
An early model of a program used to test ideas
quiz.e: Prototypes are built to get feedback.

quiz.q: What is the binary representation of the decimal number 13?
What is the decimal value of the binary number 10000?
quiz.e: The 1 is in the 16s place.

quiz.q: Why does adding one more bit to a representation double the number of values it can represent?
o: Bits become twice as large when another bit is added
Each additional bit can be either 0 or 1, doubling the combinations
One bit holds two bytes, so the capacity doubles
It does not, because each new bit adds only one more value
quiz.e: 2^(n+1) is twice 2^n.

quiz.q: A music file is compressed using a method that removes sounds humans cannot easily hear. This is:
o: Lossy compression
Lossless compression
Encryption
Sampling
quiz.e: Some data is permanently discarded.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of a pattern a program might find in a data set?
o: Sales tend to rise every December
A file name
The number of bits
A password
quiz.e: Patterns are regularities across data.

quiz.q: A data set contains duplicate entries for some customers. Before analyzing, the analyst should:
o: Ignore them
Delete all data
Encrypt it
Remove or merge the duplicates
quiz.e: Duplicates would distort counts.

quiz.q: Which of the following is metadata for a digital photo?
o: The pixels in the photo
The photographer's opinion
The time and location it was taken
The photo's colors
quiz.e: Metadata describes the data.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements about algorithms is true?
o: Every problem has exactly one algorithm that can solve it
Algorithms only work on numbers and cannot process text
Algorithms must always use loops in order to work
Different algorithms can solve the same problem at different speeds
quiz.e: Efficiency varies between algorithms.

quiz.q: Iteration in an algorithm means:
o: Choosing between steps
Repeating steps
Running steps once in order
Ending a program
quiz.e: Loops implement iteration.

quiz.q: A binary search is performed on a sorted list of 8 items. What is the maximum number of items that need to be checked?
quiz.e: Each check halves the list: 8, 4, 2, 1 gives up to 4 checks.

quiz.q: The traveling salesperson problem is often solved with a heuristic because:
o: Finding the exact best route takes unreasonably long for many cities
It is easy to solve exactly, but heuristics are simply faster
It has no solution, so only an approximation can be given
It cannot be simulated by a computer for large numbers of cities
quiz.e: The number of routes grows explosively.

quiz.q: Which statement best describes why the Internet can continue working when a router fails?
o: Data can be rerouted along other paths
Failed routers repair themselves instantly
A central computer fixes it
Packets are no longer needed
quiz.e: Redundancy provides alternatives.

quiz.q: A parallel solution has a part that must run sequentially. How does that affect the overall speedup?
o: It increases the speedup without limit
It has no effect
It makes the program fail
It limits the speedup
quiz.e: The sequential part cannot be sped up.

quiz.q: An app uses data from users to recommend content. Which concern is most relevant?
o: The color scheme of the app and how it looks on a screen
The speed of the keyboard that the user types on
The weight of the device that the app is running on
Privacy and how the data is used and shared
quiz.e: Collected data can reveal personal information.

quiz.q: Which is an example of a beneficial effect of computing on society?
o: Increased cyberbullying
Identity theft
Data breaches
Online access to medical information
quiz.e: Computing can expand access to information.

quiz.q: Why might a school choose an open-source tool?
o: The code cannot be changed, so it stays the same for everyone
It is always faster than any other kind of software
The code can be examined and adapted, and it often costs less
It has no license, so anyone can claim the code as their own
quiz.e: Open-source licenses allow reuse and modification.

o: Nothing
quiz.e: 3 > 4 is false, so the else branch displays y.

The ability of a system to handle growth in data or users.

Encryption that uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt.
Encryption using a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt.

Software that records what a user types.

A version of HTTP that encrypts web traffic.

Unfair outcomes from a program because of biased data or design.
Getting ideas, data or work from a large group of people, often online.
Research in which volunteers help collect or analyze data.
A set of licenses that let creators allow certain uses of their work.
Software whose source code is available for anyone to view and modify.
Presenting another person's work as your own.
Creations of the mind, such as writing, art and code, protected by law.
A result of a computing innovation that its creators did not plan.
The amount of energy used by computing devices and data centers.

PART_A.q: A programmer is testing a program and finds that it gives incorrect results for some inputs but never crashes. Which type of error is most likely?
o: Syntax error
Runtime error
Logic error
Overflow error
PART_A.e: The code runs but does not do what was intended.

PART_A.q: Which of the following best describes the advantage of testing a program with feedback from a diverse group of users?
o: It guarantees no errors
It helps find problems and improve usability for different people
It makes the code shorter
It speeds up the processor

PART_A.q: A team writes comments explaining each procedure in a program. The most likely benefit is that:
o: Other programmers can understand and maintain the code
The program runs faster
The computer reads the comments
The program uses fewer bits

PART_A.q: A computer uses 6 bits to store each integer. What is the largest value it can store?
An 8-bit value represents how many different possibilities?
A student stores the colors of a traffic light (red, yellow, green) using binary codes. What is the minimum number of bits needed?
PART_A.e: Three values need at least 2 bits (4 codes).

PART_A.q: Which of the following would be most appropriate for lossy compression?
o: A spreadsheet of financial data
A vacation photo for a website
A program's source code
A legal contract
PART_A.e: Slight loss in a photo may not be noticeable.

PART_A.q: Increasing the number of bits used per pixel in an image will most likely:
o: Allow more colors to be represented and increase the file size
Reduce the file size
Reduce the number of colors
Have no effect
PART_A.e: More bits mean more possible colors and more data.

PART_A.q: A researcher finds that students who eat breakfast have higher test scores. Which is the most appropriate conclusion?
o: Eating breakfast is associated with higher scores, but other factors may be involved
Breakfast causes higher scores
Test scores cause students to eat breakfast
Breakfast has no effect
PART_A.e: Correlation alone does not prove causation.

PART_A.q: Which of the following is an advantage of analyzing a very large data set using a computer?
o: The data is always unbiased
No data cleaning is needed
Privacy is no longer a concern
Patterns can be found that would be hard to see otherwise
PART_A.e: Computers can process massive amounts of data.

PART_A.q: A city combines anonymous transit data with public social media posts. Which risk does this most directly raise?
o: The data will be compressed
The network will be faster
Individuals might be identified
The data will be lost

PART_A.q: Which of the following algorithms must be able to be built from sequencing, selection and iteration?
o: Only search algorithms
Only sorting algorithms
Any algorithm
Only recursive algorithms
PART_A.e: These three constructs are sufficient for all algorithms.

PART_A.q: A sorted list has 100 elements. Which statement about searching it is true?
o: Linear search will always be faster
Binary search will generally be faster than linear search
They take exactly the same time
Binary search cannot be used

PART_A.q: For which problem is a heuristic most appropriate?
o: Finding a good, but not necessarily perfect, route for a delivery truck with many stops
Adding two numbers
Checking if a number is even
Counting items in a list
PART_A.e: Exact solutions would take too long.

 count ← count + 2

PART_A.q: Which of the following is true of the way data is sent on the Internet?
o: Data is divided into packets that can take different paths
Data is sent in one piece along a fixed path
Data always takes the shortest route
Data is stored by a central server

PART_A.q: A network has a bandwidth of 8 megabits per second. About how long will it take to download a 24 megabit file?
o: 192 seconds
32 seconds
0.33 seconds
3 seconds

PART_A.q: Which of the following best explains why the Internet is considered fault tolerant?
o: Every device is connected to a central server
Devices never fail
Data can be rerouted if part of the network fails
Packets are never lost

PART_A.q: A user receives an email asking for their password. The email link goes to a site that looks like their bank. This is most likely:
o: A denial-of-service attack
Encryption
Phishing
Compression
PART_A.e: It is an attempt to steal credentials.

PART_A.q: Which of the following describes public-key encryption?
o: The same key encrypts and decrypts
A public key encrypts and a different private key decrypts
No key is needed
Only the sender has a key

PART_A.q: Which of the following provides the strongest account protection?
o: A strong password plus a code sent to the user's phone
A short password
A password that is shared
A password written on the device
PART_A.e: Two factors are harder to compromise.

PART_A.q: Which of the following is an example of the digital divide?
o: Students in a rural area lack reliable Internet access for online classes
A student uses two devices
A website is popular
A phone has a camera

PART_A.q: A group of volunteers helps classify images of galaxies online. This is an example of:
o: Lossy compression
A denial of service
Encryption
Citizen science and crowdsourcing

PART_A.q: A programmer wants to include a photo in an app and the photo is licensed under Creative Commons with attribution required. What must the programmer do?
o: Remove the creator's name
Claim the photo as their own
Give credit to the creator as required by the license
Do nothing

PART_A.q: A facial recognition program is less accurate for some groups. What is the most likely cause?
o: The camera is too fast
The training data did not represent all groups well
The program uses too few comments
The Internet is slow
PART_A.e: Biased data leads to biased results.

PART_A.q: Which of the following is a potential harmful effect of a computing innovation?
o: Loss of privacy from collection of personal data
Faster communication
Cheaper storage
More access to information

PART_B1.q: A student develops a program in small pieces, testing each piece before adding the next. This approach is called:
o: Incremental development
Lossy compression
Parallel computing
Sampling
PART_B1.e: It makes problems easier to isolate.

PART_B1.q: Which of the following would best help a programmer determine why a loop runs one too many times?
o: Compressing the program
Encrypting the data
Running it with no input
Hand-tracing the loop with sample values
PART_B1.e: Tracing shows where the count goes wrong.

PART_B1.q: A text message is stored using 8 bits per character. How many bits are needed to store a 10-character message?
Which of the following numbers cannot be represented using 4 bits?
A music app stores songs using lossless compression. Which is a consequence?
o: The audio is permanently degraded
The original audio can be restored exactly
The file is always smaller than lossy
The song cannot be played

PART_B1.q: A company collects data about which pages users visit. The company wants to protect privacy. Which action helps most?
o: Collecting more data
Removing personally identifiable information before analysis
Sharing the data publicly
Keeping user names

PART_B1.q: A spreadsheet contains a column of ages. Which operation would produce only the rows with ages above 21?
o: Filtering
Sorting
Concatenating
Compressing
PART_B1.e: Filtering selects rows that meet a condition.

PART_B1.q: Which of the following describes an algorithm that runs in unreasonable time?
o: The number of steps doubles each time one item is added to the input
The number of steps equals the number of items
The number of steps is the square of the number of items
The number of steps is constant

PART_B1.q: Which of the following situations is best addressed using a simulation?
o: Calculating a total
Sorting names
Spell checking
Predicting how traffic will flow if a new road is built
PART_B1.e: Simulations test scenarios without building them.

PART_B1.q:
What is displayed?

x ← 1
REPEAT 3 TIMES
{
 x ← x * 3
}
DISPLAY(x)

PART_B1.e: Two values, 4 and 7, are greater than 3.

PART_B1.q: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a parameter in a procedure?
o: It stores the procedure's result
It allows the procedure to work with different values each time it is called
It names the procedure
It ends the procedure

PART_B1.q: A 90 megabyte file is sent at 6 megabytes per second. How many seconds will the transfer take?
A task takes 120 seconds sequentially. Two processors can split it perfectly. About how long will it take in parallel?
o: 60 seconds
240 seconds
120 seconds
30 seconds
PART_B1.e: Splitting equally across two processors halves the time.

PART_B1.q: Which of the following is true of DNS?
o: It encrypts packets
It compresses web pages
It stores user passwords
It maps names like example.com to IP addresses
PART_B1.e: It lets people use names instead of numbers.

PART_B1.q: A website uses HTTPS. Which of the following is a benefit?
o: The site loads instantly
The site is free from malware
The site cannot be copied
Data sent between the user and the site is encrypted

PART_B1.q: Why can a public key safely be shared with anyone?
o: It cannot be used for anything
It is the same as the private key
It can only encrypt, and only the private key can decrypt
It never changes
PART_B1.e: Knowing the public key does not reveal the private key.

PART_B1.q: A social media site recommends content based on what a user has liked in the past. A possible negative effect is that:
o: Users see no content
The site becomes slower for everyone
Users may see mostly content that matches their existing views
Users lose their passwords

PART_B1.q: Which of the following is an example of open-source collaboration?
o: A company keeping its code secret
Developers around the world contributing improvements to shared code
A student copying a program without credit
A website selling software

PART_B1.q: A school installs sensors that record student attendance with facial recognition. Which concern is most relevant?
o: Privacy and the risk of bias in the system
The color of the cameras
Battery life
The shape of the sensor

PART_B2.q: An image is 100 pixels wide and 100 pixels tall, and each pixel uses 24 bits. How many bits are needed to store the image without compression?
A sound is sampled 10 times per second using 8 bits per sample. How many bits are needed to store 5 seconds?
A binary search is used on a sorted list of 64 items. What is the maximum number of comparisons?
PART_B2.e: 64 halves to 1 in 6 steps (64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 is 7 items checked), so at most 7 comparisons.

PART_B2.q:
What is displayed?

n ← 2
REPEAT UNTIL (n > 50)
{
 n ← n * n
}
DISPLAY(n)
PART_B2.e: n becomes 4, 16, then 256; the loop stops when n exceeds 50.

PART_B2.q: Which expression is true if a number n is divisible by 3?
o: n MOD 3 = 3
n MOD 2 = 0
n MOD 3 = 0

PART_B2.q: A computer program takes 100 seconds on one processor. A parallel version has 20 seconds that must run sequentially and 80 seconds that can be split among 4 processors. How long will the parallel version take?
o: 25 seconds
100 seconds
60 seconds
40 seconds

PART_B2.q: A file is 600 megabits and the connection is 20 megabits per second. How many seconds will it take?
A user wants to send a private message to someone they have never met. Which method allows this without first sharing a secret?
o: Symmetric encryption with a shared key
No encryption
Public-key encryption
Compression
PART_B2.e: The recipient's public key can be shared openly.

PART_B2.q: A city uses data from smartphones to plan bus routes. Which is the most important concern to address?
o: Choosing a bus color
Counting buses
Protecting residents' privacy and ensuring all neighborhoods are represented
Naming routes
PART_B2.e: Data from phones may leave out people without them.

PART_C.q: Written response: choose TWO concepts from different units and construct an argument connecting them. Cite specific evidence from each.
o: Names both concepts precisely, gives concrete evidence for each, and explains the causal/logical bridge
Lists the two topics without connecting them
Describes only one concept in detail
Gives a personal opinion with no course evidence
PART_C.e: Strong responses anchor every claim in specific unit content.

PART_C.q: Essay plan: identify the single most important takeaway of this course. Defend it using three units as evidence, then address one counterargument.
o: Clear thesis, three unit-specific pieces of evidence, genuine counterargument, resolution
Thesis with no support
Topic list with no argument
Anecdote unrelated to course content
PART_C.e: Full argumentative architecture earns top marks.

workedExamples.title: Binary to decimal
workedExamples.prompt: Convert the binary number 101101 to decimal.
steps: Write the place values from the right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
Mark the places with a 1: 32, 8, 4 and 1.

workedExamples.title: Decimal to binary
workedExamples.prompt: Convert the decimal number 37 to binary.
steps: Find the largest power of 2 that fits: 32, leaving 5.
Next, 4 fits into 5, leaving 1; then 1 fits.
Place 1s at 32, 4 and 1 and 0s elsewhere: 100101.

workedExamples.title: How many bits are needed?
workedExamples.prompt: A game has 90 different characters. What is the minimum number of bits needed to give each character a unique binary code?
steps: With n bits you can represent 2^n values.
2^6 = 64 is too few, and 2^7 = 128 is enough.
So 7 bits are needed.

workedExamples.title: File size of an image
workedExamples.prompt: A 200 by 100 pixel image uses 24 bits per pixel. How many bytes does it take without compression?
steps: Number of pixels: 200 x 100 = 20,000.

workedExamples.title: Tracing a loop
workedExamples.prompt: What does this code display? total ← 0; FOR EACH n IN [3, 5, 8]: IF (n MOD 2 = 1): total ← total + n; DISPLAY(total).
steps: Check each value: 3 is odd, 5 is odd, 8 is even.
Add the odd numbers: 3 + 5.
Display the total.

workedExamples.title: MOD for even or odd
workedExamples.prompt: Write a condition that is true when n is odd, and explain it.
steps: An odd number leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2.
So n MOD 2 = 1 is true for odd numbers.
For n = 7, 7 MOD 2 = 1, which is true.

workedExamples.title: Binary search steps
workedExamples.prompt: How many comparisons does binary search need at most to find an item in a sorted list of 1,000 items?
steps: Each comparison halves the remaining items.
Count how many halvings reduce 1000 to 1: 500, 250, 125, 63, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 is about 10.
So at most about 10 comparisons.

workedExamples.title: Download time
workedExamples.prompt: A 450 megabyte file is downloaded at 15 megabytes per second. How long does the download take?
steps: Time equals file size divided by bandwidth.
State the units.

workedExamples.title: Speedup with parallel processors
workedExamples.prompt: A task takes 80 seconds sequentially. In a parallel version, 10 seconds must run sequentially and the other 70 seconds split evenly among 7 processors. What is the speedup?
steps: Parallel time: 10 + 70 / 7 = 20 seconds.
Speedup = sequential time / parallel time.

hardQuiz.q: A program passes all of its tests but still gives wrong results for some real users. Which is the most likely reason?
o: Tests cannot find errors, so passing tests proves nothing
The tests did not include the inputs that cause the problem
The program has a syntax error that the tests did not check
The users made a mistake when they entered their data
hardQuiz.e: Passing tests only shows correctness for the cases tested.

hardQuiz.q: Which is the best reason to document and comment a program during development?
o: It helps collaborators and future maintainers understand and modify the code
It makes the program run faster because the computer reads it
It removes the need for testing because the code is explained
The computer requires it before it will run the program

hardQuiz.q: A system stores each of 300 different product IDs using the fewest bits possible. How many bits per ID are required?
hardQuiz.e: 2^8 = 256 is too small and 2^9 = 512 is enough.

hardQuiz.q: A student increases the sampling rate of a recording from 8,000 to 16,000 samples per second and keeps the same bits per sample. What happens to the file size?
o: It approximately doubles
It halves
It stays the same
It quadruples
hardQuiz.e: Twice as many samples means twice as many bits.

hardQuiz.q: A study of a city's bike share program finds that neighborhoods with more bike stations have higher property values. Which statement is best supported?
o: Bike stations cause property values to rise in a neighborhood
The two variables are related, but a third factor such as wealth may explain both
Higher property values cause the city to build more bike stations
The data prove that no relationship exists between the variables

hardQuiz.q: Which of the following is the main reason that combining data sets can create privacy risks even when each set is anonymized?
o: Anonymized data is always made public after it is shared
Combining data sets deletes details from each of the sets
It makes the data smaller so that fewer details are stored
Matching details across the sets can identify individuals
hardQuiz.e: Quasi-identifiers like age and zip code can single people out.

hardQuiz.q: A programmer must search a list of 1,000,000 unsorted names once. Which approach is most efficient?
o: Binary search without sorting
Sorting first and then using binary search for a single search
Searching only the first half
Linear search
hardQuiz.e: For a single search, sorting costs more than scanning.

hardQuiz.q: Which of the following best explains why the best-known algorithms for some problems are considered unreasonable?
o: The number of steps grows exponentially with the input size
They use too many variables for a computer to store
They can only be run on parallel computers with many processors
They are written in pseudocode instead of a real language
hardQuiz.e: Exponential growth makes large inputs infeasible.

hardQuiz.q:
What is displayed?

x ← 5
y ← x
x ← 8
DISPLAY(y)
hardQuiz.e: y was assigned the value 5, and later changing x does not change y.

hardQuiz.q:
What is displayed?

a ← 2
b ← 3
REPEAT 2 TIMES
{
 a ← a + b
 b ← a - b
}
DISPLAY(b)
hardQuiz.e: First pass: a = 2 + 3 = 5 and b = 5 - 3 = 2. Second pass: a = 5 + 2 = 7 and b = 7 - 2 = 5, so b is 5.

hardQuiz.q: A message is split into packets that arrive out of order. Which statement correctly describes what happens?
o: The message is discarded because the packets were out of order
The message arrives scrambled and cannot be read by the receiver
The packets are reassembled in the correct order at the destination
The sender must resend the entire message in the correct order
hardQuiz.e: Packets include information that allows reordering.

hardQuiz.q: A program has 30 seconds of sequential work and 60 seconds of work that can be perfectly divided among 6 processors. What is the speedup compared with running all 90 seconds sequentially?
o: About 2.25

hardQuiz.q: Which of the following best explains why a website using HTTPS can still be unsafe for the user?
o: HTTPS removes all passwords so no site can steal them
Encryption protects data in transit but the site itself may be malicious
HTTPS slows down the Internet so users avoid unsafe sites
HTTPS is not encryption, so data can be read in transit
hardQuiz.e: Encryption does not verify that the site is trustworthy.

hardQuiz.q: In public-key encryption, Alice wants to prove a message came from her. Which key should she use?
o: Her public key only, so that anyone can read the message
Bob's private key, so that he can confirm it was sent by her
Her private key, so others can verify it with her public key
No key at all, because the message is signed by her name
hardQuiz.e: Digital signatures use the private key to sign and the public key to verify.

hardQuiz.q: A hospital uses an algorithm trained on data that came mostly from one demographic group. Which outcome is most likely?
o: The algorithm may perform worse for other groups
The algorithm will be unbiased because computers cannot be unfair
The algorithm will run slower on the data from other groups
The algorithm will become open source because of the data
hardQuiz.e: Unrepresentative training data leads to uneven accuracy.

hardQuiz.q: Which of the following would most reduce the digital divide in a community?
o: Providing affordable Internet access and devices
Building a faster server for the community's websites
Making websites more colorful and attractive to visitors
Adding more advertisements to pay for online content
